items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Erroll Garner had Don Byas, Slam and Specs Powell in a quartet.

ctx.x: By this time, the Bebop movement was catching on, having started on 52nd Street with musicians like Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie. There were only a few big bands going, mostly playing theatres. The Ballrooms were still open but usually had small combos. Even the Savoy Ballroom was no longer a place which interested me. The atmosphere was no longer the same. Things were bad economically, and they were starting to tax the dance halls very heavily after the war. Also, Bebop was hard music to dance to, a fact…

The only interesting thing musically that happened for me on during the next few weeks was a concert/the 9th of June at the Town Hall. This concert was presented by my old friend Timmie Rosenkrantz, and the line up was another who's who inthe jazz world. Red Norvo had an orchestra composed of Joe (Flip) Phillips, Shorty Rodgers, Aaron Sachs, Eddie Bert, Remo Palmieri, Teddy Wilson and Slam Stewart. A fellow named Fran Warren did a voice and drum solo. Don Byas and Slam Stewart did a couple of duets. Erroll Garner…

In July, I was engaged by George Johnson to play one month in the Savoy in Boston. A nice blowing little fellow named Johnny Hartsfield was the tenor man and Red Richards was the pianist. Both of them had been in New York for quite some time, but it was the first time I had met them. Johnny was a nice guy until he had taken a few drinks, and then he was a little devil.
